title: Quantifying the Mechanical Properties of the Endothelial Glycocalyx with Atomic Force Microscopy
protocol: Clean glass slides in piranha solution for 15 min.
Wash cleaned glass slides with distilled water.
Bake the washed glass slides to dry them.
Coat glass slides with aminopropyl triethoxy silane (APTES) in a vacuum deposition chamber.
Cut a silicone gasket using a Silhouette SD cutting tool.
Prepare the flow chamber for cell growth by controlling its dimensions.
Align the top piece of the flow chamber with the gasket in the cell culture dish.
Secure the alignment with a magnetic ring.
Fill the assembly with isopropyl alcohol (IPA) for sterilization.
Assemble the full flow system.
Connect the flow ports in the cell culture dish to three-way valves.
Connect the valves to open 30 ml syringes.
Flush IPA through the entire system.
Wash the system with 30 ml of McCoy's medium containing 4% Fetal Calf Serum (FCS).
Fill the system with 20 ml of Vec Technologies cell growth medium.
Place covers on top of the syringes.
Insert a needle in the catch reservoir syringe cap to move medium back to the feed reservoir.
Attach sterile 0.2 μm filters to the air inlets in the covers.
Remove the growth medium from the T25 Flask containing HUVECs and Vec Technologies' growth medium.
Release the monolayer of cells with 2 ml of 2.5% trypsin.
Quench the trypsinization by adding 10 ml of cell culture medium to the flask once cells are in solution.
Centrifuge the cell suspension for 5 minutes.
Remove the supernatant from the centrifuged cells.
Resuspend the cells in 1 ml of cell culture medium containing serum.
Load the cell suspension (0.5 ml, ~50,000 cells) into a syringe.
Inject the cell suspension into the flow chamber through a three-way valve.
Allow the cells to settle and adhere to the glass substrate for 2 hr before initiating flow.
Grow the adhered cells under flow in an incubator at 37 °C for 1 to 5 days until confluent.
Clean tipless AFM cantilevers in nitric acid for 5 min.
Functionalize the cantilevers with aminopropyl triethoxy silane (APTES) in a vapor deposition chamber.
Prepare a solution of 5 mg/ml NHS-sulfo-LC-biotin in Hank's Buffered Salt Solution (HBSS).
Submerge the cantilevers in the biotin solution for 15 min to conjugate the silane with N-Hydroxysuccinimide (NHS) chemistry.
Incubate 20 ml of Vec Technologies cell culture medium, including serum, with 200 μl of streptavidin beads for 12 hr.
Remove the streptavidin beads from the medium using a magnet.
Filter the biotin-free medium through a 0.22 μm sterile filter.
Wash the flow chamber and cells in 37 °C biotin-free medium.
Prepare a stock solution of 1 μl of 2.4 μm streptavidin-coated beads in 1 ml of biotin-free medium.
Add 100 μl of the bead stock to the cell culture dish.
Pick up streptavidin beads with the cantilever by landing on the glass surface next to a bead.
Retract the tip and position it over the bead.
Press the cantilever down onto the bead and rest for several seconds.
Measure the sensitivity of the cantilever by indenting onto bare glass.
Use the slope of the curve to set the tip deflection as a function of voltage.
Calculate the spring constant of the cantilever from thermal calibration in MFP3D software.
Use the calibrated cantilever to indent samples.
Position the cantilever over a cell near the nucleus.
Set the cantilever height approximately 3 μm above the cell surface using a soft approach.
Set the software for 20 repeated indentations at a rate of 1 μm/sec to a maximum force of 7 nN.
